# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2024_ciprofol"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2024_ciprofol"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13121> (CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems
  Pharmacology 13(5):823-836, open access; PMCID PMC11098162)

The supplement carries the study summary (Table S1), the covariate screen
(Table S2), the model-building steps (Table S3), the loading-dose simulation
table (Table S4) and the final NONMEM control stream. The control stream's
`$THETA`, `$OMEGA` and `$SIGMA` blocks hold initial estimates; every value in
the model comes from the final estimates in Equation 3 and Table 2 of the main
text, and the control stream is used only for the model structure and the
coding of the categorical covariates. No erratum or correction notice was found
(PubMed and the journal landing page, checked 2026-10-29).

# Population

Liu 2024 pooled 12 clinical trials of ciprofol (HSK3486): six phase 1 studies in
healthy volunteers (three in Australia, three in China), four phase 2/3 studies
in Chinese adults undergoing elective surgery, and two studies (HSK3486-205 and
HSK3486-307) in Chinese adults on mechanical ventilation sedated in the
intensive care unit (Table S1). The analysis data set held 3918 plasma
concentrations from 462 subjects (Table 1): 125 healthy volunteers, 225 surgical
patients and 112 ICU patients; median age 38 years (18-77), median weight
61.7 kg (41.6-97.9), 51.1% female, 85.3% Asian. The ICU patients were older
(median 57 vs 32 years) and had lower total protein than the non-ICU subjects.
Blood was sampled venously in 230 subjects, arterially in 146 and at both sites
in 86. Doses ranged from single injections of 0.128-0.9 mg/kg to induction
boluses followed by maintenance infusions of up to 24 h; the ICU studies used a
0.1-0.2 mg/kg loading dose and a 0.3 mg/kg/h initial maintenance rate titrated
within 0.06-0.8 mg/kg/h.

The same information is available programmatically via the model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("Liu_2024_ciprofol")()$population`).

# Typical-value replication

The paper simulates a typical 33-year-old, 62 kg patient and five extreme
patients after a 0.1 mg/kg loading dose over 4 min followed by 0.3 mg/kg/h for
24 h, and reports AUC0-24h and Cmax for each (Results 'Impact of body weight and
age on exposure'; Figure S6). The reference covariate levels of Equation 3 are
those of a male ICU patient in a long-term infusion study with arterial
sampling, which is what these simulations use. The extreme patients are
18 and 77 years at 62 kg, and 40, 85 and 116 kg at 33 years.

The covariate sensitivity analysis (Results 'Covariate sensitivity analysis';
Figure S5) changes one categorical covariate at a time from the same typical
patient: a non-ICU patient (AUC0-24h +20.9%, Cmax +8.97%), venous sampling
(AUC0-24h +16.9%, Cmax +7.43%) and female sex (an exposure change of less than
7.1%).

```{r typical-events}
mod <- readModelDb("Liu_2024_ciprofol")

scenarios <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,          ~WT, ~AGE, ~SEXF, ~SAMPLE_ARTERIAL, ~DIS_CRITILL,
  "Typical",           62,   33,     0,                1,            1,
  "Youngest (18 y)",   62,   18,     0,                1,            1,
  "Oldest (77 y)",     62,   77,     0,                1,            1,
  "Underweight (40 kg)", 40, 33,     0,                1,            1,
  "Overweight (85 kg)",  85, 33,     0,                1,            1,
  "Obese (116 kg)",   116,   33,     0,                1,            1,
  "Non-ICU",           62,   33,     0,                1,            0,
  "Venous sampling",   62,   33,     0,                0,            1,
  "Female",            62,   33,     1,                1,            1
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), REGIMEN_CONTINF = 1)

ld_dur <- 4 / 60  # h
make_regimen <- function(cov, ld_mgkg, ld_dur, md_mgkgh, md_dur, obs_times) {
  dose <- bind_rows(
    cov |> mutate(time = 0, amt = ld_mgkg * WT, rate = amt / ld_dur),
    cov |> mutate(time = ld_dur, amt = md_mgkgh * WT * md_dur, rate = md_mgkgh * WT)
  ) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = cov$id, time = obs_times) |>
    left_join(cov, by = "id") |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |> arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

obs_grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 1 / 60), ld_dur)))
ev_typ <- make_regimen(scenarios, 0.1, ld_dur, 0.3, 24, obs_grid)

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_typ,
                           returnType = "data.frame", atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10) |>
  select(-any_of("scenario")) |>
  left_join(scenarios |> select(id, scenario), by = "id")
```

```{r typical-figure, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure S6 of Liu 2024: typical-value concentration-time profiles for the typical 33-year-old, 62 kg patient and the extreme ages and weights (left panel 0-24 h, right panel 0-20 min)."}
fig_s6 <- sim_typ |>
  filter(scenario %in% scenarios$scenario[1:6])
p1 <- ggplot(fig_s6, aes(time, Cc, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Ciprofol (ng/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
p2 <- ggplot(filter(fig_s6, time <= 20 / 60), aes(time * 60, Cc, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Ciprofol (ng/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
p1
p2
```

# PKNCA validation

AUC0-24h and Cmax are computed with PKNCA from the typical-value profiles, one
group per scenario.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, scenario, time, Cc)
# Time-zero guarantee (the observation grid already starts at 0).
nca_conc <- bind_rows(
  nca_conc,
  nca_conc |> distinct(id, scenario) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, scenario, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, time)

nca_dose <- ev_typ |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, scenario, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | scenario + id,
                             concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | scenario + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result)
stopifnot(nrow(nca_tbl) == 2 * nrow(scenarios))
```

## Comparison against published values

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,               ~auclast, ~cmax,
  "Typical",                   4606, 500.3,
  "Youngest (18 y)",           4608, 513.7,
  "Oldest (77 y)",             4602, 461.0,
  "Underweight (40 kg)",       3638, 353.6,
  "Overweight (85 kg)",        5424, 635.3,
  "Obese (116 kg)",            6345, 796.5
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_tbl |> filter(scenario %in% published$scenario),
  reference = published,
  by = "scenario",
  units = c(auclast = "ng*h/mL", cmax = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Typical-value AUC0-24h and Cmax, simulated vs Liu 2024 Results 'Impact of body weight and age on exposure'. * differs from the reference by more than 20%.")
```

```{r nca-gate}
check <- nca_tbl |>
  filter(scenario %in% published$scenario) |>
  select(scenario, PPTESTCD, Simulated = PPORRES) |>
  inner_join(
    published |> pivot_longer(-scenario, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "Reference"),
    by = c("scenario", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Simulated - Reference) / Reference)

# Deterministic (zeroRe, fixed covariates): the only differences are rounding
# of the published parameters and the AUC integration, so a 1% bound is safe
# and still catches any mis-transcribed parameter or covariate effect.
stopifnot(
  nrow(check) == 12L,
  !anyNA(check$pct_diff),
  all(abs(check$pct_diff) < 1)
)
```

The covariate-sensitivity contrasts are expressed relative to the typical
patient, exactly as the paper reports them.

```{r sensitivity}
sens <- nca_tbl |>
  select(scenario, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(
    auc_pct = 100 * (auclast / auclast[scenario == "Typical"] - 1),
    cmax_pct = 100 * (cmax / cmax[scenario == "Typical"] - 1)
  ) |>
  filter(scenario %in% c("Non-ICU", "Venous sampling", "Female")) |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~scenario,         ~pub_auc_pct, ~pub_cmax_pct,
      "Non-ICU",                 20.9,          8.97,
      "Venous sampling",         16.9,          7.43,
      "Female",                    NA,            NA
    ),
    by = "scenario"
  )

sens |>
  select(scenario, auc_pct, pub_auc_pct, cmax_pct, pub_cmax_pct) |>
  rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario,
    "AUC0-24h change, simulated (%)" = auc_pct,
    "AUC0-24h change, published (%)" = pub_auc_pct,
    "Cmax change, simulated (%)" = cmax_pct,
    "Cmax change, published (%)" = pub_cmax_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Covariate sensitivity relative to the typical patient (Liu 2024 Results 'Covariate sensitivity analysis'; the paper gives only '< 7.1%' for sex).")

stopifnot(
  abs(sens$auc_pct[sens$scenario == "Non-ICU"] - 20.9) < 0.5,
  abs(sens$cmax_pct[sens$scenario == "Non-ICU"] - 8.97) < 0.5,
  abs(sens$auc_pct[sens$scenario == "Venous sampling"] - 16.9) < 0.5,
  abs(sens$cmax_pct[sens$scenario == "Venous sampling"] - 7.43) < 0.5,
  # Female clearance is higher, so exposure falls, and by no more than 7.1%.
  sens$auc_pct[sens$scenario == "Female"] < 0,
  abs(sens$auc_pct[sens$scenario == "Female"]) < 7.15,
  abs(sens$cmax_pct[sens$scenario == "Female"]) < 7.15
)
```

# Virtual ICU cohort

Figures 4 and 5 and Table S4 simulate the ICU sedation regimens in mechanically
ventilated patients. The paper does not print the covariates of the simulated
patients; the cohort below follows the ICU column of Table 1 (median weight
63.5 kg, range 42-90; median age 57 years, range 19-77; 39.3% female; 93.75%
sampled arterially only) and holds the two study-level indicators at the ICU
long-term-infusion levels.

The same 150 virtual patients receive every regimen, as in the paper (its
0.2 mg/kg column of Table S4 is exactly twice its 0.1 mg/kg column). Their
random effects are drawn in base R from the model's `omega` and passed to the
solver as parameters, so the cohort does not depend on rxode2's per-thread
random-number streams.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20240305)
n_per_arm <- 150

icu <- tibble(
  k = seq_len(n_per_arm),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_per_arm, log(63.5), 0.17), 42), 90),
  AGE = pmin(pmax(round(rnorm(n_per_arm, 57, 14)), 19), 77),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_per_arm, 1, 0.393),
  SAMPLE_ARTERIAL = rbinom(n_per_arm, 1, 0.9375),
  DIS_CRITILL = 1,
  REGIMEN_CONTINF = 1
)
omega <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)$omega
eta <- matrix(rnorm(n_per_arm * nrow(omega)), n_per_arm) %*% chol(omega)
colnames(eta) <- rownames(omega)

arms_ld <- tidyr::expand_grid(ld_mgkg = c(0.1, 0.2), ld_min = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)) |>
  mutate(md_mgkgh = 0.3, family = "Loading-dose duration")
arms_md <- tidyr::expand_grid(ld_mgkg = c(0.1, 0.2), md_mgkgh = c(0.06, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.8)) |>
  mutate(ld_min = 4, family = "Maintenance rate")
arms <- bind_rows(arms_ld, arms_md) |> mutate(arm = row_number())

md_dur <- 25  # h, Methods 'Target concentration'
ev_icu <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  a <- arms[i, ]
  cov <- icu |> mutate(id = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm + k)
  ld_h <- a$ld_min / 60
  make_regimen(cov, a$ld_mgkg, ld_h, a$md_mgkgh, md_dur,
               sort(unique(c(seq(0, 25, by = 0.25), ld_h, ld_h + md_dur)))) |>
    mutate(arm = a$arm)
}))

stopifnot(all(table(ev_icu$arm[ev_icu$evid == 0]) > 0),
          length(unique(ev_icu$id)) == nrow(arms) * n_per_arm)

# One row of random effects per simulated id; patient k carries the same etas
# in every arm.
id_k <- distinct(ev_icu, id, k)
params <- data.frame(id = id_k$id, eta[id_k$k, , drop = FALSE])
```

# Simulation

Individual predictions (`Cc`) are compared with the paper, which reports
model-predicted concentrations without residual error.

```{r simulate}
sim_icu <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_icu, params = params,
                           returnType = "data.frame", keep = "arm") |>
  left_join(arms, by = "arm")
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Liu 2024: a 0.1 mg/kg loading dose over 0.5-5 min followed by 0.3 mg/kg/h (median and 5th-95th percentile of the individual predictions). Red lines: median and 5th-95th percentile of the target concentration (143.3; 77.0-215.6 ng/mL)."}
target <- c(lo = 77.0, mid = 143.3, hi = 215.6)
fig4 <- sim_icu |>
  filter(family == "Loading-dose duration", ld_mgkg == 0.1) |>
  group_by(ld_min, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(fig4, aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target["mid"], colour = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target[c("lo", "hi")], colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("LD duration", ld_min, "min")) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Ciprofol (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r fig5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Liu 2024: a 0.1 mg/kg loading dose over 4 min followed by 0.06-0.3 mg/kg/h (median and 5th-95th percentile of the individual predictions)."}
fig5 <- sim_icu |>
  filter(family == "Maintenance rate", ld_mgkg == 0.1, md_mgkgh <= 0.3) |>
  group_by(md_mgkgh, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(fig5, aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target["mid"], colour = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = target[c("lo", "hi")], colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("MD", md_mgkgh, "mg/kg/h")) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Ciprofol (ng/mL)") +
  theme_bw()
```

## Concentration at the end of the loading dose (Table S4)

Table S4 prints the median simulated concentration at the end of the loading
infusion. Two cells are defective in the source: the 0.5 min, 0.1 mg/kg median
is printed as 127 ng/mL although its own '% change' column (593% of the
215.6 ng/mL upper target) and the 0.2 mg/kg row (2556 ng/mL, twice the dose)
both imply about 1278 ng/mL, and the 5 min, 0.2 mg/kg median is missing. Both
are shown but not gated.

```{r table-s4}
ld_end <- sim_icu |>
  filter(family == "Loading-dose duration", abs(time - ld_min / 60) < 1e-9) |>
  group_by(ld_mgkg, ld_min) |>
  summarise(Simulated = median(Cc), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~ld_mgkg, ~ld_min, ~Published,
      0.1, 0.5,  NA,
      0.1, 1,  1059,
      0.1, 2,   732,
      0.1, 3,   572,
      0.1, 4,   464,
      0.1, 5,   388,
      0.2, 0.5, 2556,
      0.2, 1,  2119,
      0.2, 2,  1463,
      0.2, 3,  1143,
      0.2, 4,   928,
      0.2, 5,    NA
    ),
    by = c("ld_mgkg", "ld_min")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (Simulated - Published) / Published)

ld_end |>
  rename("Loading dose (mg/kg)" = ld_mgkg, "Duration (min)" = ld_min,
         "Simulated median (ng/mL)" = Simulated, "Published median (ng/mL)" = Published,
         "% difference" = pct_diff, "Subjects" = n) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median concentration at the end of the loading-dose infusion, simulated vs Liu 2024 Table S4.")

gated <- filter(ld_end, !is.na(Published))
stopifnot(
  nrow(gated) == 10L,
  all(gated$n == n_per_arm),
  # Centre: a wrong V1, age effect or unit moves every row together.
  abs(median(gated$pct_diff)) < 10,
  # Envelope across rows, robust to which subjects land in the tails.
  quantile(abs(gated$pct_diff), 0.9) < 20
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Direction of the sex effect.** The Results text states that "Women exhibited
  9.31% lower CL compared to men". Equation 3 (`+0.089 * sex = female`), the
  Table 2 factor of 1.09 for female sex and the sex panel of Figure 1 all show
  female clearance 9.3% *higher* than male, and only that direction reproduces
  the sensitivity statement that sex changes exposure by less than 7.1% (the
  simulation above gives about -7.1% for AUC0-24h). The model follows the
  equation.
* **"35.1% lower" clearance in short-term non-ICU studies.** The Results text
  says clearance was 35.1% lower in short-term infusion non-ICU studies than in
  long-term ICU studies. Equation 3 and Table 2 give
  exp(0.229 - 0.237) = 0.992 for that combination, essentially no difference,
  and the Figure 1 study-design panel shows short-term studies with *higher*
  clearance. 35.1% equals 1 - 0.789 x 0.823, the ICU factor multiplied by the
  venous-sampling factor, so the sentence appears to combine the wrong pair of
  effects. The model follows the equation.
* **Inverted indicator coding.** The paper's flags are the complements of the
  package's canonical covariates: its `ICU` flag is 1 for the non-ICU studies,
  `FLG` is 1 for short-term infusion studies, and `SITE0` is 1 for venous
  samples. The model keeps the paper's coefficients and signs and applies them
  to `1 - DIS_CRITILL`, `1 - REGIMEN_CONTINF` and `1 - SAMPLE_ARTERIAL`, so the
  typical values are those of an arterially sampled ICU patient in a long-term
  infusion study, as in the paper.
* **Study design is a study-level flag.** `REGIMEN_CONTINF` follows the paper's
  per-study assignment (HSK3486-102, -204, -205, -306 and -307 are long-term
  infusion studies), not the duration of each individual dose. Its effects on
  V2 (x 0.125) and V3 (x 0.198) are large, so simulating a regimen that was not
  studied requires a choice of level; the ICU sedation simulations here use the
  long-term level.
* **Sampling site is per record.** In the NONMEM `$PK` block the venous flag
  changes clearance on each record, so a subject sampled at both sites has a
  clearance that switches between records. The model reproduces this when
  `SAMPLE_ARTERIAL` is supplied per observation row. The simulations above hold
  it constant per subject.
* **IIV and residual magnitudes.** Table 2 prints IIV and residual variability
  in percent. The control stream's `$OMEGA` and `$SIGMA` values are the squares
  of those percentages to within the last digit, so the percentages are read as
  log-scale standard deviations and squared to give the variances.
* **ICU cohort.** The covariates of the patients simulated for Figures 4 and 5
  and Table S4 are not reported. The cohort above is drawn to match the ICU
  column of Table 1; its weight and age distributions are assumptions.
* **Table S4 defects.** Two cells of Table S4 are unusable (see above) and are
  not used in the gate.
* **Exposure-safety analysis.** The logistic regression of hypotension on
  exposure is described only as showing no clinically meaningful relationship,
  with no coefficients reported ("data not shown"), so there is no
  exposure-response model to encode.
